title: Lument Closes $30.7 Million Fannie Mae Refinance for D.C. Affordable Housing
summary: Lument has closed two Fannie Mae loans totaling $30.7 million to refinance a portfolio of seven affordable multifamily housing communities in Washington, D.C. Lument’s John Hurley, a director based in D.C., led the transaction.
body_text: New York, NY — March 25, 2026 — Lument has closed two Fannie Mae loans totaling $30.7 million to refinance a portfolio of seven affordable multifamily housing communities in Washington, D.C. Lument’s John Hurley, a director based in D.C., led the transaction. The properties were constructed between 1948 and 1965 and have been substantially renovated since current ownership acquired the assets. All units are occupied by tenants using the Housing Choice Voucher Program, administered by the District of Columbia Housing Authority (DCHA) as part of its efforts to provide quality, affordable housing options to D.C. residents. “Replacing bank debt with favorable Fannie Mae financing puts these important affordable housing communities in a strong position to continue serving its residents for many years to come,” said Lument’s Hurley. Both Fannie Mae loans have a fixed rate and 10-year term with interest only for five years. “The team at Lument delivered a truly excellent outcome, from a smooth and seamless underwriting process to obtaining maximum proceeds at closing,” said borrower Craig London. The sponsorship team, led by Mr. London, has been acquiring, redeveloping, owning, and managing conventional and affordable multifamily housing in the D.C. area for approximately 15 years. This was a brokered transaction, brought to Lument through Christopher Davis with Metropolitan Capital. About Lument Lument, a subsidiary of ORIX Corporation USA, is a national leader in commercial real estate finance and delivers a comprehensive set of capital solutions customized for investors in multifamily, affordable housing, and seniors housing and healthcare real estate. Lument offers Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, FHA, USDA, and balance sheet financing, as well as a full suite of capital market lending products. In addition, Lument provides a suite of real estate advisory solutions including real estate investment sales, investment banking, and investment management solutions. The company has approximately 550 employees in over 30 offices across the United States. Securities, investment banking, and advisory services are provided through Lument Securities, LLC, member FINRA/SIPC. Lument Investment Management, LLC, is registered as an investment adviser with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. For more information, visit https://www.lument.com/.

title: What Documents Do You Need for a Loan Against Mutual Funds?
summary: Learn what documents and digital checks are usually needed for a loan against mutual funds, why the process is simpler than traditional loans, and what to keep ready.
body_text: What Documents Do You Need for a Loan Against Mutual Funds? Intro If you are considering a loan against mutual funds, the paperwork question usually comes before the rate question: what do I need to keep ready? The short answer is that a modern loan against mutual funds is less about carrying a folder of documents and more about completing a few digital checks. You generally need identity/KYC readiness, access to your mutual fund holdings, bank or auto-pay setup, and the ability to complete the pledge and agreement flow. That matters because the real benefit is not just getting a loan. It is getting liquidity without selling the mutual funds you built over time. Key Takeaways A loan against mutual funds usually depends on KYC, holdings verification, pledge setup, bank or auto-pay setup, and agreement signing. The exact requirement can vary by lender and eligibility, so avoid assuming every case uses the same checklist. A digital LAMF flow can be simpler than selling investments or applying for a generic personal loan, especially if your mutual fund records are ready. The short answer: keep your KYC, holdings, and bank details ready For most investors, the practical checklist starts with three things: your identity, your mutual fund portfolio, and your repayment setup. You should be ready to complete KYC, verify or fetch your holdings, set up the required mandate or auto-pay instruction, and sign the loan agreement digitally. In Yenmo’s app-led flow, the broad process includes KYC, pledge setup, auto-pay, and agreement signing inside the app. The exact screens and checks can vary based on your portfolio and lending partner. But the direction is clear: the process is designed around digital verification, not branch visits and physical paperwork. If you are still learning the category, Yenmo’s complete guide to loans against mutual funds is a useful starting point. Do you need physical mutual fund statements? Usually, the better question is whether your holdings can be verified digitally. Many investors think they need to download every statement, print forms, and manually prove ownership. In an app-led LAMF flow, the important step is connecting or verifying the holdings that can be pledged, not producing paperwork for its own sake. That is why your mutual fund records should be clean and accessible. If your folios, demat holdings, or account details are outdated, the borrowing process can feel slower even if the loan product itself is digital. The smoother your investment records are, the easier it becomes to treat your portfolio as a source of liquidity without redeeming it. What digital checks should you expect? You should expect checks that confirm who you are, what you own, and how the repayment arrangement will work. Common digital steps in this kind of flow may include KYC, DigiLocker-style document access where required, bank verification, mandate or auto-pay setup, pledge confirmation through the relevant mutual fund infrastructure, and agreement signing. Yenmo’s trust layer includes names investors may already recognise, such as CAMS, KFin, NSDL, and DigiLocker, along with lending partners including Bajaj Finance, Tata Capital, and DSP Finance. These signals matter because a loan against mutual funds is not only a credit decision. It is also an operational trust decision. The point is not to memorise every back-end step. The point is to know that the process should make ownership, pledge, and repayment terms clear before you proceed. Why this is different from selling your mutual funds When you redeem mutual funds, you turn investments into cash. That can feel simple, but it may interrupt compounding, trigger tax or exit-load considerations, and force you out of the market when you may still want to stay invested. A loan against mutual funds solves a different problem. It lets you pledge eligible holdings and borrow against them, so the portfolio can remain invested while you handle the cash need. That does not mean borrowing is always the right answer. It means the document and setup process should be compared against the cost of selling too early, not against an imaginary zero-friction option. You can also use Yenmo’s loan against mutual fund calculator vs redemption calculator to think through the cost of borrowing versus redeeming. What can slow down your application? A digital process can still slow down if your records are not ready. Watch for these common friction points: your KYC details are outdated your mobile number or email does not match investment records your bank details need verification your mutual fund holdings are not eligible or are harder to pledge the lender needs extra checks before sanctioning the facility you do not complete the auto-pay or agreement step correctly None of this means the process is broken. It simply means that a pledge-backed loan depends on clean ownership and repayment information. Should you apply before or after a cash need becomes urgent? If you already know you may need liquidity, it is usually better to understand eligibility before the need becomes stressful. That does not mean you should borrow without a reason. It means checking eligibility can help you know whether your portfolio can support a credit line before you are forced into a rushed redemption. This is one reason Yenmo’s “check eligibility” flow is useful. It helps you understand the borrowing route while your investments are still intact, instead of waiting until selling feels like the only option. FAQ Do I need income proof for a loan against mutual funds? Requirements can vary by lender and eligibility. Because the loan is backed by eligible mutual fund holdings, the portfolio and pledge process are central, but you should verify the exact requirement in the app before relying on any generic checklist. Do I need to submit physical documents? A modern LAMF flow is designed to be digital, but exact document access and verification steps can vary. Expect KYC, holdings verification, auto-pay setup, pledge confirmation, and agreement signing rather than a traditional branch-heavy process. Can I apply if my mutual funds are held across platforms? It may be possible depending on how the holdings are recorded and whether they are eligible for pledge. The practical step is to check eligibility rather than assume all holdings will be treated the same way. What is the most important thing to keep ready? Keep your KYC, phone/email records, bank details, and mutual fund holding records up to date. Clean records make a digital pledge-backed loan easier to process. Conclusion A loan against mutual funds should not feel like a paperwork maze. The practical checklist is simple: be KYC-ready, make sure your holdings can be verified, complete the pledge flow, set up repayment instructions, and sign the agreement clearly. The exact details may vary by lender, but the overall job is the same: unlock liquidity without forcing a sale of your investments. If you need cash but still want your mutual funds working for you, check your eligibility with Yenmo and compare that option before redeeming units too early.

title: Inside nonprofits using AI to extend their impact
summary: Discover how nonprofits are applying AI to strengthen communities, expand opportunity, and create lasting impact across the globe.
body_text: An animal shelter is forecasting where foster homes will be needed before “kitten season” hits its peak. Researchers studying a neurodegenerative disease that affects hundreds of thousands of people are accelerating progress toward treatments and cures. A small nonprofit is spending more time mentoring young people and less time buried in paperwork. These stories don’t have much in common on the surface, but together, they point to a broader shift: AI is helping nonprofit organizations across the globe tackle some of society’s most pressing challenges. Animal Protection Denmark, Answer ALS, and Everything Suarve are three nonprofits that turned to Microsoft to solve different problems. Today, AI is helping them expand opportunity, strengthen communities, and create new possibilities for the people, animals, and causes they serve—extending their impact far beyond what their size or resources might otherwise allow. Learn more about how Microsoft helps nonprofits accelerate their missions Animal Protection Denmark: From guesswork to insight in kitten care Every year, Animal Protection Denmark prepares for “kitten season,” when shelters see a surge in vulnerable animals needing care. As the organization grew, so did the volume of data flowing across shelters, foster networks, volunteers, and supporters. Teams often spent long hours every month reconciling information from different systems, making it harder to forecast needs and coordinate resources. Using Microsoft data and AI capabilities, Animal Protection Denmark unified that data into a single source of truth. Teams can identify trends earlier, forecast demand for foster placements, and monitor shelter capacity in real time. Staff can also access complete records for each animal, helping ensure continuity of care and supporting faster adoption decisions. By combining a unified data foundation with AI-powered insights, Animal Protection Denmark spends less time managing information and more time acting on it. The result is earlier planning, faster decisions, and better outcomes for the animals that depend on them. Read how Animal Protection Denmark expands its impact with Microsoft Answer ALS: Turning data into discovery Answer ALS was created to accelerate progress toward treatments and a cure for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a progressive neurodegenerative disease that affects over 450,000 people worldwide. Together with Microsoft, the organization built Neuromine, one of the world’s largest ALS research hubs, bringing together trillions of data points contributed by more than 2,500 people living with the disease. Azure AI Search powers Neuromine’s query function so researchers can quickly learn details about an individual’s disease trajectory or even their DNA, which helps pinpoint cell lines to further study. Additionally, Answer ALS is developing a chatbot in Microsoft Foundry that uses generative AI to answer user questions and direct researchers to relevant data. Before Neuromine, researchers often spent months, and sometimes more than a year, assembling data and biological samples before meaningful analysis could begin. Today, researchers around the world can access hundreds of patient lines and related clinical data in hours rather than months, helping them move more quickly from questions to insights. By making high-quality research data easier to explore, share, and build upon, Answer ALS is helping accelerate research by as much as 65% over the next few years. The platform is enabling researchers around the world to collaborate more effectively, uncover new patterns in the data, and advance the search for better treatments and, ultimately, a cure. Discover how Answer ALS is progressing toward treatments and cures with Microsoft Azure Everything Suarve: Scaling second chances with AI Everything Suarve helps young people in Australia rebuild their lives through job training, mentorship, mental health support, and practical life skills. Many participants arrive after facing challenges such as housing insecurity, unstable home environments, or trauma. For a small team, the work depends on trust, consistency, and showing up for young people when they need support most. As demand for its programs grew, so did the administrative burden. Referrals arrived through emails, paper forms, and phone calls, while staff tracked participant progress across disconnected systems. To streamline operations, Everything Suarve used Microsoft data and AI capabilities to build a solution that centralizes enrollment, case management, reporting, and communications. The organization also uses Microsoft 365 Copilot to help with grant writing, document summarization, and other administrative tasks, reducing the time spent on manual work. Today, Everything Suarve’s staff can manage referrals, case notes, reporting, and participant communications in a single workflow. The new platform saves up to eight hours per participant during enrollment, while Copilot reduces grant application work by as much as two weeks. By automating processes and putting AI to work, Everything Suarve is reducing administrative overhead and creating more time to help young people build confidence, skills, and a path forward toward employment, education, and long-term stability. See how Everything Suarve helps young people thrive with Microsoft What other nonprofits can learn from these stories These three organizations serve different communities and pursue different goals. Yet together they show that organizations create the most value from AI when they use it to strengthen human expertise and start with a problem worth solving or a mission worth advancing. At Animal Protection Denmark, staff can spot needs before they peak. At Answer ALS, researchers are compressing years of discovery into months. At Everything Suarve, staff spend less time on forms and more time with young people rebuilding their lives. Together, these stories reflect a broader shift already underway across organizations of every size. AI is becoming part of how decisions are made, how services get delivered, and how people work. Success is no longer defined by the technology alone. It comes from combining technology with human judgment, experience, and purpose. We call this Frontier Transformation : to move beyond isolated tools and individual tasks to rethink how they achieve their mission. Sometimes the result is greater efficiency. Often, it creates something more meaningful: the ability to reach more people, respond more quickly, and extend impact in ways that were previously out of reach. As AI becomes more accessible, these nonprofits are showing that meaningful transformation is not reserved for the largest enterprises. It can begin anywhere people are willing to pair innovation with a clear sense of purpose. Explore how Microsoft Elevate for Nonprofits can help expand social impact

title: 10 Best Profound Alternatives for 2026
summary: Comparing Profound alternatives on execution, coverage, and price for agencies, startups, and enterprise teams.
body_text: Last verified July 2026. This category ships weekly, so I re-check pricing and engine coverage on every update. The best Profound alternatives are Writesonic for tracking plus execution, Peec AI for agencies with growing teams, and Ahrefs Brand Radar for large-scale research. Otterly.AI offers the lowest credible paid entry price, while AthenaHQ provides the most useful free sampler. Cheapest: Otterly.AI at $29 per month. Best for agencies: Peec AI, because every paid plan includes unlimited seats. Disclosure: I'm Samanyou Garg, founder and CEO of Writesonic, which I ranked first here. Pricing here reflects our July 2026 verification pass. Vendors in this category change plans often, so confirm current terms before you buy. Key takeaways The real difference is execution. Profound has moved beyond reporting with Projects and Aim. The decision now comes down to how mature each action system is, how much work it can complete, and what happens after it finds a gap. Writesonic ranks first because its autonomous marketing agents combine AI visibility and SEO data, then carry work through content, outreach, technical fixes, approval, and measurement. Its limitation is a steeper first week than a focused tracker. Profound remains a strong choice. It has the category's best-known analytics product, broad enterprise coverage, a polished interface, and substantial customer evidence. It also ships fast. Self-serve engine coverage can hide the real bill. Profound Starter tracks ChatGPT. Growth adds Perplexity and Google AI Overviews. Shopping and broader engine access require Enterprise. Seat economics matter for agencies. Peec AI and SE Visible include unlimited users, while Profound Growth includes three seats. Third-party coverage deserves its own workflow. Muck Rack's May 2026 study found that earned media accounts for 84% of all AI citations. Muck Rack cofounder and CEO Greg Galant said, "For communications teams, that is validation that the work they do to earn coverage in the right outlets has real consequences beyond traditional metrics." Profound alternatives at a glance Rank Tool Best for Entry price Engines tracked Main limitation 1 Writesonic Teams that want tracking and execution together $99 monthly for tracking ChatGPT, AI Overviews, Gemini on self-serve; more on higher plans Monthly action allowance depends on the plan 2 Peec AI Affordable tracking for smaller teams $95 monthly Three selected models on self-serve; more available Extra engines can increase the bill 3 Ahrefs Brand Radar One-off market research, not daily monitoring $199 monthly per AI index AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot Several indexes become expensive 4 Otterly.AI The lowest-cost place to start $29 monthly ChatGPT, AI Overviews, Perplexity, Copilot on base plans Several engines cost extra 5 AthenaHQ Testing several engines before buying Free credit sampler Several engines sampled from the free allocation Paid access jumps to $295 monthly 6 Scrunch AI Sitecore and enterprise DXP teams $300 monthly Major answer engines; confirm the list in trial AXP has limited availability 7 Searchable European small and mid-sized teams $125 monthly Confirm engine list in trial; docs conflict Engine documentation needs confirmation 8 Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit Existing Semrush or Adobe customers $99 monthly, billed annually Varies by plan and domain count Shopping requires an enterprise product 9 SE Visible Simple tracking for large teams $99 monthly ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Overviews, AI Mode, Perplexity Weekly refresh and CSV-only exports Why teams look for a Profound alternative Profound is the reference point for this category. It deserves that position. The company has shipped a lot in a short period. Projects arrived on June 26, 2026, followed by Aim on July 2. Projects converts findings into ranked work. Aim runs in the background, turns signals into tasks, and measures movement. That's a genuine closed loop. Ads Studio followed in July as an invite-only, ChatGPT-focused beta. Shopping analysis now reaches individual products and merchants. Profound is clearly building past the dashboard. Teams still compare alternatives for four practical reasons. The action system is new Projects and Aim have existed for weeks, rather than years. They may become excellent. Today, buyers have less public evidence about how the loop performs across long-running programs, larger teams, and repeated approval cycles. That's a maturity question. Profound already has stronger analytics evidence than most competitors. It also has financial backing. Fortune reported in February 2026 that Profound raised a $96 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $155 million. Funding proves that serious investors believe in the category and the company. It doesn't tell a marketing team how much work will get completed next month. Agent credits cap every self-serve plan Profound Starter is listed at $99 per month billed annually and includes 100 agent credits. Growth is listed at $399 per month billed annually and includes 400 credits. Those limits matter because agent work is the part buyers increasingly care about. A report can run every week without changing a page, earning a citation, or resolving a crawler problem. Each executed action has a cost in credits. Before buying, ask Profound to map a representative month of work to its credit model. Use your own backlog. A generic product demonstration won't show whether the allowance fits your program. Engine coverage is tiered Starter includes ChatGPT, 50 tracked prompts, and one seat. Growth includes ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews, with 100 prompts and three seats. Enterprise expands coverage to as many as nine engines and adds Shopping, SSO, SAML, and SOC 2 support. This structure can work well for a focused program. It becomes restrictive when a self-serve team needs Gemini, shopping results, broader model coverage, or enterprise controls without entering a custom sales process. Off-site execution remains the harder problem A brand can edit its own website whenever it wants. It can't directly edit the publisher pages, comparison articles, Reddit discussions, and earned-media coverage that answer engines cite. That's why outreach depth matters. Ask each vendor to walk you through five things: Which third-party page to target Who the right author or editor is How it prepares contact-specific outreach Where the response gets recorded How it measures the citation change afterward Profound has citation analysis, Agents, Sheets, Projects, and Aim. I haven't found public evidence showing author-contact citation outreach, deep user-generated-content targeting, or automatic site-audit fixes at the same level of detail. Given their release pace, that could change by the time you read this. Trial terms aren't published Profound doesn't publish trial terms. That's different from having no trial. Ask what data you can import, how many prompts you can test, which engines are included, whether agent credits are available, and whether you can export results before the evaluation ends. Those details determine whether a trial can answer the buying question. How I evaluated these Profound alternatives I compared the products against the job a buyer hires them to do. The methodology uses six criteria. Execution depth. I looked at how far each product carries a finding through prioritization, production, approval, delivery, and later measurement. Engine coverage. I checked the engines available on the entry plan and separated self-serve access from enterprise access. A long engine list means little when the engines a team needs sit behind a custom contract. SEO connection. AI citations still depend heavily on searchable pages, technical access, authority, and external coverage. Products received more credit when they connected answer data to those inputs. Data usefulness. Large indexes help with discovery. Tracked prompts help with repeated measurement. Those are different jobs. I scored them separately and skipped the biggest-number contest. Customer evidence. Named outcomes, a substantial independent review base, and long-running deployments count more than a logo page. Small review samples are shown with their counts. Real cost. I compared prompt allowances, engines, seats, domains, refresh frequency, agent credits, and required add-ons alongside the advertised price. The ranking favors products that finish more of the work. A team that already has analysts, writers, PR support, and developers has a fair case for weighting reporting depth higher. 1. Writesonic: best for execution depth, tracking from $99 per month The product tracks ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, and Gemini across all three self-serve plans. It combines that visibility data with SEO data, then uses autonomous marketing agents to act on the findings. That execution layer is the reason I ranked my company first. The agents can prepare or update content, pursue third-party mentions, address technical issues with approval, and measure what changed. Best for: Marketing teams and agencies that need a detected visibility gap turned into completed content, outreach, or technical work. Key features: Tracks ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, and Gemini across all three self-serve plans Combines AI visibility data with SEO data Prepares and updates content through autonomous marketing agents Pursues third-party mentions through an outreach agent Addresses technical issues with approval and measures what changed Pricing: Starter costs $99 monthly or $79 per month annually and includes 50 prompts. Basic costs $249 monthly or $199 per month annually with 100 prompts. Growth costs $499 monthly or $399 per month annually with 200 prompts. Enterprise pricing is custom. The seven-day trial requires no card. Rating: G2 listed Writesonic at 4.7 out of 5 across about 2,214 reviews in July 2026 . Pros: Playbooks store repeatable workflows, Grids support bulk analysis, and tasks coordinate work and approvals. AI ad visibility and shopping results sit in the same system. Neil Patel Digital moved its AI visibility work off Profound and onto Writesonic, while Maestra went from 0% to 31% AI visibility and closed a $350K enterprise deal. Cons: The $99 entry price buys the tracking layer. The monthly action allowance depends on the plan. A system this wide takes longer to learn than a focused dashboard. Choose it when: You've already found the gaps. You can't get through them. 2. Peec AI: best for affordable tracking for smaller teams, from $95 per month Peec AI is a tracking-focused product, and it does that job well at a low price. It tracks major answer engines on daily or weekly schedules and reports mentions, citations, and competitor movement without much setup. Unlimited seats on every paid plan is the other reason smaller teams like it. Strategists, analysts, and client stakeholders can all get access without the per-seat maths that makes other tools expensive. It fits teams early in their AI visibility work more than teams running a full execution program. Best for: Smaller teams and agencies starting AI visibility work who want solid tracking at a low price with seats included. Key features: Tracks major answer engines on daily or weekly schedules Supports multiple projects Provides shopping analysis and reporting connections Offers an API on qualifying plans Identifies page, editorial, source, and user-generated-content opportunities through Actions Pricing: Starter costs $95 per month and includes unlimited users. Pro costs $245 per month and includes unlimited users. Advanced costs $495 per month and includes unlimited users. Enterprise pricing is custom. A seven-day trial is available, although current card requirements aren't stated. Rating: G2 showed Peec AI at 4.9 out of 5 across 12 reviews in July 2026 . Pros: Every paid plan includes unlimited seats. Daily or weekly tracking gives teams a choice of reporting schedule. TechCrunch reported in November 2025 that Peec AI raised a $21 million Series A. Cons: Self-serve plans include three selected models, and another model costs extra. Actions identify and prioritize work, but the team still owns final execution. The G2 rating comes from a thin sample of 12 reviews. Choose it when: Your client and user count grows faster than your prompt count. 3. Ahrefs Brand Radar: best for one-off market research, from $199 per month Brand Radar's strength is its prebuilt indexes. A team can research brands, domains, citations, topics, and competitors across large collections of AI answers and Google surfaces without defining every prompt first. Treat it as an exploration tool rather than a monitoring one. Brand Radar reads like an extension of Ahrefs' keyword explorer pointed at AI answers, which makes it strong for a market-mapping exercise and weak as the thing you open every morning. It won't run your day-to-day program, and it won't act on what it finds. Best for: Existing Ahrefs customers running a one-off market-mapping exercise, alongside a separate tool for daily monitoring and action. Key features: Researches brands, domains, citations, topics, and competitors through prebuilt indexes Searches large collections of AI answers and Google surfaces Reveals recurring publishers and competitor appearances Identifies topics for smaller daily tracking programs Connects research to search, web, Reddit, YouTube, and TikTok data Pricing: Each AI index starts at $199 per month. The bundle containing all indexes costs $699 per month. Custom prompt packages start at $50 per month. Trial terms aren't stated in this comparison. Rating: G2 listed Ahrefs at 4.5 out of 5 across about 710 reviews in July 2026 . Pros: Prebuilt indexes let teams research a market before defining every prompt. Ahrefs connects the work to familiar search and web data. Crunchbase describes Ahrefs as bootstrapped , which helps explain its product-led buying model and long focus on search data. Cons: Core chatbot indexes refresh monthly. Estimated impressions use Google search demand as a proxy instead of measured AI query volume. The price climbs when a team combines several indexes, custom prompts, and the wider Ahrefs suite. Choose it when: You need to understand the market before committing to a fixed prompt set. 4. Otterly.AI: best for the lowest-cost start, from $29 per month Otterly.AI has the lowest ongoing paid entry price here, and it's built for tracking rather than execution. Its Lite plan covers basic prompt monitoring, and higher plans add capacity, reporting, and data access. For an SMB or a team running its first AI visibility experiment, that's often the right amount of tool. You get real answer data at a price that doesn't need a business case. The product tracks brand mentions, citations, sentiment, and competitor appearances. It also monitors ChatGPT ads, shopping cards, and advertising within Google AI Overviews. Best for: Small teams that want credible monitoring and downloadable reporting without a three-figure starting bill. Key features: Tracks brand mentions, citations, sentiment, and competitor appearances Monitors ChatGPT ads and shopping cards Monitors advertising within Google AI Overviews Provides citation-change reports and query fan-out analysis Offers exports, an API, and an MCP server Pricing: Lite costs $29 per month. Standard costs $189 per month. Premium costs $489 per month. Enterprise pricing is custom. The seven-day trial doesn't require a card. Rating: G2 listed Otterly.AI at 4.8 out of 5 across 42 reviews in July 2026 . Pros: It has the lowest ongoing paid entry price in this list. Citation-change reports and query fan-out analysis help explain why a visibility score moved. Exports, an API, and an MCP server make data available outside the dashboard. Cons: Google AI Mode, Gemini, and Claude require add-ons. Advertising and shopping tools report appearances but don't manage campaigns, product feeds, merchants, or individual SKUs. Execution support is thinner than in products built around action workflows. Choose it when: You need dependable monitoring now and can run the resulting work elsewhere. 5. AthenaHQ: best free sampler, then $295 per month AthenaHQ's Essential allocation provides 300 free credits. It's the most useful free sampler here. Most free tiers hand you one static score. This one lets you inspect several engines. The paid product goes further. It supports citation analysis, crawler-access work, content tasks, on-page changes, off-page actions, and publishing connections such as Shopify. Best for: Teams that want to test several engines and an action workflow before committing budget. Key features: Uses the Essential allocation to sample several engines Provides citation analysis Supports crawler-access work and content tasks Handles on-page changes and off-page actions Connects to publishing systems such as Shopify Pricing: Essential includes 300 free credits. Starter costs $295 per month. Enterprise pricing is custom. API access and additional credits may increase the total. Separate trial terms aren't stated in this comparison. Rating: G2 showed AthenaHQ at 4.9 out of 5 across 34 reviews in July 2026 . Pros: The free allocation supports a more useful evaluation than a single static score. The paid product covers both analysis and action workflows. FinSMEs reported in June 2025 that AthenaHQ raised $2.2 million in seed funding from Y Combinator and other investors. Cons: Nothing sits between the free allocation and the $295 Starter plan. Ecommerce support doesn't reach the SKU, merchant-share, or paid-placement detail offered by dedicated shopping products. API access and additional credits may increase the total. Choose it when: You need a meaningful evaluation before procurement and can tolerate the jump to the paid plan. 6. Scrunch AI: best for agent-readiness infrastructure, from $300 per month Scrunch AI approaches the problem at the delivery layer. Its Agent Experience Platform, or AXP, can present approved site content in a format designed for automated agents. That's a different form of execution. A marketing action tool changes content, citations, or technical settings. Scrunch also addresses the infrastructure through which automated systems receive the content. Best for: Sitecore customers and enterprise DXP teams responsible for how approved content reaches automated agents. Key features: Presents approved site content to automated agents through AXP Provides answer monitoring Analyzes citations and manages prompts Reports automated-agent traffic Produces content recommendations Pricing: Starter costs $300 monthly or $250 per month annually. Growth costs $500 monthly or $417 per month annually. Enterprise pricing is custom. The seven-day trial doesn't require a card. Rating: No G2 rating cited in this comparison. Pros: AXP addresses the infrastructure through which automated systems receive content. Sitecore acquired the company in 2026, and The acquisition announcement said Scrunch served more than 500 brands and agencies. Bloomberg reported that the transaction was worth about $225 million, although neither company confirmed that figure publicly. Cons: AXP remains in limited availability. It can require more technical involvement than a conventional marketing dashboard. Its value depends on whether agent-facing delivery is a real infrastructure priority for your company. Choose it when: Your problem sits inside the DXP and delivery stack, especially if Sitecore already runs that stack. 7. Searchable: best for European teams, from $125 per month Searchable has built most of its traction in Europe, and small and mid-sized European teams make up a large share of its base. Its founding team is unusually visible on LinkedIn, which is how a lot of buyers in that market first come across it. On product, it reports on individual products, prices, ratings, merchants, categories, and how often each appears. That detail helps a retail team separate three different problems: the brand doesn't appear, the right product doesn't appear, or another merchant wins the placement. Best for: European small and mid-sized teams that want self-serve product and merchant reporting. Key features: Analyzes individual products, prices, ratings, and merchants Reports categories, platforms, and appearance frequency Shows which sellers surface in product carousels through merchant-share reporting Supports prompt research, planning, and content briefs Provides schema recommendations, technical task assignment, and early paid-placement tracking Pricing: Pro costs $125 per month. Scale costs $400 per month. Enterprise costs $999 per month. Further controls use custom pricing. The 14-day trial doesn't require a card. Rating: No G2 rating cited in this comparison. Pros: Product Gallery provides product-level and merchant-level reporting. Merchant-share reporting distinguishes brand, product, and seller-placement problems. PR Newswire reported in May 2026 that the company secured $14 million in a round led by Headline at an $85 million valuation. Cons: Its pricing FAQ and comparison table conflict on engine availability. Buyers need to confirm the exact engines in the trial. Public materials don't show direct author outreach, Reddit execution, or automatic CMS publishing. Choose it when: Product-level shopping data matters more than a broad organic marketing system. 8. Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit: best for existing Semrush and Adobe teams, from $99 per month The toolkit reports brand mentions, cited sources, topics, sentiment, competitors, and estimated AI traffic. Custom prompt tracking adds repeated position measurement, although it covers fewer answer surfaces than the broader mention reports. Its main advantage is context. Existing Semrush users can view AI visibility beside keyword, competitor, content, and site data. Best for: Organizations that already rely on Semrush for search work or Adobe for enterprise content delivery. Key features: Reports brand mentions, cited sources, topics, and sentiment Tracks competitors and estimated AI traffic Adds repeated position measurement through custom prompt tracking Displays AI visibility beside keyword, competitor, content, and site data Connects eligible Adobe customers through Adobe Brand Visibility and Adobe Experience Manager Pricing: The entry toolkit costs $99 per month for one domain and 25 daily tracked prompts, billed annually. Extra domains cost $99 per month. An additional 50 prompts costs about $60 per month. Semrush One Advanced costs $549 per month. Trial terms aren't stated in this comparison. Rating: No G2 rating cited in this comparison. Pros: Existing Semrush users can keep AI visibility beside their wider search data. Its 2025 SEC filing reported fiscal 2024 revenue of $376.8 million, annual recurring revenue of $411.6 million, and annual revenue growth of 22%. Adobe agreed to acquire Semrush for about $1.9 billion, or $12 per share, according to CNBC's November 2025 report . Cons: Self-serve mention analysis covers more surfaces than custom position tracking. AI Shopping requires Enterprise AIO, and paid AI-placement tracking isn't available. Teams may need several Semrush products to connect reporting with execution. Choose it when: Keeping work inside your current search or Adobe system matters more than buying the strongest standalone product. 9. SE Visible: best for simple tracking with unlimited seats, from $99 per month SE Visible tracks ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and Perplexity. It reports brand mentions, citations, sentiment, and competitor comparisons. Every plan includes unlimited users. That makes the product attractive to agencies and internal teams with many stakeholders. Best for: Teams that want straightforward monitoring and broad user access without per-seat charges. Key features: Tracks ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and Perplexity Reports brand mentions and citations Analyzes sentiment and competitor comparisons Includes unlimited users on every plan Connects AI Search data to the wider SEO platform for existing SE Ranking customers Pricing: Basic costs $99 per month. Core costs $189 per month. Plus costs $355 per month. Enterprise pricing is custom. The ten-day trial requires a card. Rating: No G2 rating cited in this comparison. Pros: Every plan includes unlimited users. It covers five named answer surfaces. G2 listed SE Ranking at 4.7 out of 5 across about 2,396 reviews in July 2026 , although that rating applies to the parent platform and shouldn't be treated as a rating for the newer standalone product. Cons: Standalone data refreshes weekly. Exports are limited to CSV, while API and MCP access require the separate SE Ranking platform. The standalone product doesn't execute content, outreach, or technical fixes. Choose it when: Many people need access and weekly reporting is frequent enough. How Profound itself compares A fair comparison needs to state what Profound already does well. Its analytics cover prompt research, citations, competitors, sentiment, answer details, and automated-agent traffic. Higher plans add wider engine support and detailed Shopping analysis. The interface is polished, and the company has made complex answer data easier for executive teams to consume. Best for: Teams that value established analytics, executive reporting, and rapid product development. Key features: Researches prompts, citations, competitors, sentiment, and answer details Reports automated-agent traffic Uses Agents and Sheets to investigate opportunities Turns findings into managed work with Projects Adds ongoing prioritization and measurement through Aim Pricing: Starter costs $99 per month, tracks 50 prompts on ChatGPT, includes one seat, and provides 100 agent credits. Growth is listed at $399 per month billed annually, tracks 100 prompts across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews, includes three seats, and provides 400 agent credits. Agency Growth is listed at $399 per month billed annually for each client workspace. Enterprise uses custom pricing and can include broader engine coverage, Shopping, SSO, SAML, and SOC 2. Public trial terms aren't available. Rating: No G2 rating cited in this comparison. Pros: Covers analytics, managed work, prioritization, and measurement Provides wider engine support and detailed Shopping analysis on higher plans Offers a polished interface that makes complex answer data easier for executive teams to consume Cons: Projects and Aim have existed for weeks, rather than years. Agent credits cap every self-serve plan. Shopping and broader engine coverage require Enterprise. Choose it when: Established analytics and executive reporting matter more than the narrower advantages offered by the alternatives below. Published starting prices and seat constraints for a 10-person team These are minimum published plan prices, not actual ten-person totals, unless unlimited seats are explicitly noted. Seat caps, quotes, workspaces, annual billing, and add-ons all move the final number. The cleanest comparison is to separate a known bill from a buying constraint. Tool Plan used for comparison Known 10-person starting cost Important condition Writesonic Basic $249 base plus extra seats Additional Basic and Growth seats cost $50 per user Peec AI Starter $95 monthly Unlimited seats included Profound Growth At least $399 monthly Three seats included; seven more require a quote Ahrefs Brand Radar One AI index At least $199 monthly Wider index coverage and Ahrefs access can add cost Otterly.AI Lite At least $29 monthly Confirm user allowance and required engine add-ons AthenaHQ Starter At least $295 monthly Credit usage and API access can add cost Scrunch AI Starter At least $300 monthly Confirm enterprise user and AXP access terms Searchable Pro At least $125 monthly Confirm seat allowance and required shopping capacity Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit Entry toolkit At least $99 monthly One domain and annual billing at entry SE Visible Basic $99 monthly Unlimited users included Peec AI has the cleanest 10-person self-serve bill: $95 per month. SE Visible follows at $99. Profound Growth begins at $399 for three seats. A buyer needs a quote for the remaining seven users, and that same plan provides 100 tracked prompts and 400 agent credits. An agency managing separate clients should also account for the $399 monthly cost of each Agency Growth workspace. For my own product, the base plan and seat additions should be calculated together. If several people only need reports, don't buy everyone a full working seat. Ask which access level each person needs. The same rule applies across the list. A ten-person company rarely has ten daily operators. Count analysts, approvers, report viewers, external clients, and administrators separately. Then ask the vendor which roles consume paid seats. Is there a free Profound alternative? Not a permanent one, and you should be sceptical of anything advertised that way. What exists is sampling. AthenaHQ gives you a free credit allocation you can spend across several engines, which is the most useful way to see real answers about your brand before paying. Most other products run a time-boxed trial instead, so you get full features for a week or two and then choose. Free checkers are a different thing. Several vendors publish a one-off "check your AI visibility" tool that returns a single score. Those are useful for a first look and useless for tracking, because one score on one day tells you nothing about movement. AI answers vary by model, region, and rerun. If budget is the binding constraint, the honest path is a low-cost paid tracker rather than a free one. Otterly.AI starts at $29 per month, which is less than most teams spend on a single freelance article. How to switch from Profound without losing your baseline A migration should preserve the old measurement long enough to explain any change. Switching prompts, engines, locations, and tools on the same day creates noise that no dashboard can untangle. 1. Export the current operating set Save the prompts, prompt groups, competitors, cited domains, historical reports, engine settings, markets, and any open Projects. Also export a list of completed actions. That prevents the new system from recommending work your team already finished. 2. Mark the prompts that affect revenue Most accounts contain a mix of commercial prompts, category research, executive curiosities, and low-value variants. Tag the prompts tied to product discovery, vendor comparison, purchase intent, and objections. Move those first. Broad research prompts can follow after the new baseline is stable. 3. Match the measurement settings Use the same engines, locations, language, prompt wording, and schedule in both products. Keep these settings stable during the overlap period. Exact answer matching is unrealistic because generated responses vary. The goal is to compare direction across a consistent prompt set. 4. Run both systems in parallel Keep Profound and the alternative active for at least one normal reporting cycle. Compare source answers, citations, brand mentions, competitors, and the date each system collected its result. A difference isn't automatically an error. It may come from model versions, geography, account state, retrieval method, or collection time. Ask each vendor to explain the sampling method. 5. Test one real action workflow Select one content gap, one citation opportunity, and one technical issue. Follow each through to completion. Record: What the product found What it recommended What it produced itself Which approvals it required Where a person had to take over How it measured the finished work Which allowance, credit, or add-on it consumed This test reveals more than a broad feature checklist. 6. Rebuild reports after validating the data Move executive reports last. Stakeholders care about continuity, and an unexplained score change can damage confidence in the whole program. Show the old and new baselines side by side. Document the engines, prompts, cadence, and sampling differences. Then set a clear date after which the new system becomes the reporting source. 7. Cancel after checking the archive Confirm that exports open correctly, historical charts are saved, pending work has an owner, and finance knows the renewal date. If an agency workspace contains client data, store each client's export separately. Also worth a look I scored nine products in depth. Buyers in this category also shortlist Brandlight, Goodie, Cognizo, ZipTie.dev, Am I On AI, and Surfer's AI tracking. I haven't run them through the same six criteria, so I'm naming them rather than ranking them. If one of them fits a constraint the nine above don't, trial it alongside your shortlist and hold it to the same test: what does it do after it finds a gap. Which alternative fits your team Agencies with many users Choose Peec AI when seat count is the main cost driver. The $95 Starter plan includes unlimited users, and the same seat policy continues across paid plans. Choose SE Visible when clients need simpler weekly reports and unlimited access. It costs $99 per month at entry, although its standalone execution support is limited. An agency should also price client workspaces, prompt allocations, white-label reporting, exports, and approval roles. Unlimited users won't help if every client requires an expensive separate workspace. Teams that need execution capacity Choose Writesonic when the team wants one system to find a gap and carry the work through content, outreach, or technical changes. This fits organizations whose backlog grows faster than their headcount. Choose AthenaHQ when you want to sample an action workflow before paying. Its free credits make the initial evaluation easier, although the first paid plan costs $295 per month. SEO teams doing one-off market research Choose Ahrefs Brand Radar for a mapping exercise when you don't yet know which prompts, publishers, or competitors matter. Its indexes suit discovery. Pair it with something else for daily monitoring, because it reads as an extension of the keyword explorer and won't act on what it finds. The economics work best for existing Ahrefs customers. A team combining several AI indexes should compare the full bundle cost with a dedicated tracker. European small and mid-sized teams Choose Searchable if you're buying in Europe and want self-serve product and merchant reporting. Most of its base sits in that market. Profound is also strong for shopping analysis, but access sits on Enterprise. Peec AI and Writesonic include shopping visibility inside broader systems. Confirm whether you need SKU-level merchant detail or a wider brand view. Sitecore and DXP organizations Choose Scrunch AI when agent-facing content delivery is an infrastructure concern. Its position inside Sitecore makes it relevant to teams already running that stack. A marketing team that mainly wants prompt tracking will probably find a conventional tracker easier to deploy. Existing Semrush or Adobe customers Choose Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit when avoiding another vendor matters. The toolkit connects AI reporting with a familiar search suite, and Adobe customers have a route into AEM-based workflows. Check custom prompt coverage and Enterprise AIO pricing before assuming the entry toolkit covers shopping or every engine. Smaller teams and anyone just getting started Choose Otterly.AI for the lowest ongoing paid price. It provides enough monitoring and reporting to run a serious small program, provided the base engine set matches your buyers. Choose AthenaHQ when free evaluation matters more than the eventual paid price. Frequently asked questions What is the best Profound alternative? Writesonic is my top pick when execution carries the most weight. It combines AI visibility and SEO data with autonomous content, outreach, and technical workflows. Peec AI is better for agencies prioritizing unlimited seats. Ahrefs Brand Radar is better for broad research across large prebuilt answer indexes. What is the cheapest Profound alternative? Otterly.AI is the cheapest credible paid alternative at $29 per month. Its base plan covers core monitoring, but Gemini, Claude, and Google AI Mode require add-ons. AthenaHQ offers a free 300-credit sampler, although its first ongoing paid plan costs $295 per month. Which Profound alternative is best for agencies? Peec AI is the clearest agency choice because every paid plan includes unlimited seats. Starter costs $95 per month. SE Visible also includes unlimited users and starts at $99, but refreshes weekly and provides less execution support. Agencies should still compare client-workspace and prompt costs. Does Profound have an execution layer? Yes. Profound has Agents, Sheets, Projects, and Aim. Projects turns findings into ranked tasks, while Aim runs ongoing work and measures movement. These capabilities shipped in June and July 2026, so the fair concern is maturity and agent-credit capacity. The execution layer exists. Does Profound offer a free trial? Profound doesn't publish clear trial terms. That doesn't prove a trial is unavailable. Ask the sales team which engines, prompts, exports, and agent credits an evaluation includes. AthenaHQ offers a free credit sampler, while several alternatives publish fixed seven-day or fourteen-day trial terms. How much does Profound cost? Profound Starter is listed at $99 per month billed annually for ChatGPT, 50 prompts, one seat, and 100 agent credits. Growth costs $399 for three engines, 100 prompts, three seats, and 400 credits. Enterprise pricing is custom and can include broader engine coverage, Shopping, and SSO. Which alternative has the broadest research data? Ahrefs Brand Radar is the strongest choice for broad research. Its prebuilt indexes help teams examine brands, domains, topics, citations, and competitors before creating a tracked prompt set. The tradeoff is price: one AI index starts at $199 per month, while the complete bundle costs $699. Which Profound alternative is best for ecommerce? Searchable reports individual products, prices, merchants, ratings, and carousel appearances on a self-serve plan, and it's a common pick among European teams. Profound offers deep Shopping analysis on larger contracts. Writesonic and Peec AI cover shopping visibility inside broader systems, which is usually enough unless merchant-share detail is the main job. Buy around the bottleneck Profound is a serious product. It ships fast, has strong reporting, and now has a real action loop. A team with analysts and established delivery resources may prefer it over every alternative here. The deciding factor is the bottleneck inside your team. If work stalls after the report, evaluate execution. If stakeholder access drives cost, compare seats. If you haven't identified the market yet, buy research breadth. If products and merchants determine revenue, test shopping detail. Keep the same prompts during each trial. Run one action to completion. Then buy the system that removes the delay you can already see. Samanyou Garg Founder @ Writesonic Samanyou is the founder of Writesonic, a platform that helps you track & boost your brand’s visibility in AI search. Two years before the launch of ChatGPT, Writesonic was already at the forefront, helping organizations automate their entire marketing workflow through specialized AI agents for SEO and content. Samanyou is a Forbes 30 Under 30 awardee and a winner of the 2019 Global Undergraduate Awards, often referred to as the junior Nobel Prize.

title: Fresenius Medical Care kündigt neues Aktienrückkaufprogramm mit einem Gesamtvolumen von rund 1 Milliarde Euro und einer schrittweisen Umsetzung über 12 Monate an
body_text: Pressemitteilung Das Gesamtvolumen des Aktienrückkaufprogramms beträgt rund 1 Milliarde Euro über einen Zeitraum von 12 Monaten Der Aktienrückkauf soll in naher Zukunft beginnen Bad Homburg (26. Mai 2026 ) – Fresenius Medical Care (FME), der weltweit führende Anbieter von Produkten und Dienstleistungen für Menschen mit Nierenerkrankungen, beabsichtigt die Durchführung eines neuen Aktienrückkaufprogramms mit einem Gesamtvolumen von rund 1 Milliarde Euro. Das Programm soll in Tranchen über einen Zeitraum von 12 Monaten ab seinem Start umgesetzt werden. Das Aktienrückkaufprogramm basiert auf der Ermächtigung zum Erwerb und zur Verwendung eigener Aktien, die von der Hauptversammlung der Gesellschaft am 21. Mai 2026 erteilt wurde. Es soll in naher Zukunft beginnen – nur wenige Wochen nach dem erfolgreichen Abschluss des vorherigen Aktienrückkaufprogramms am 30. April 2026. Als Teil des Kapitalallokationsrahmens von FME ergänzen regelmäßige Aktienrückkaufprogramme die Dividendenzahlungen und spiegeln den anhaltenden Fokus des Unternehmens auf disziplinierte Kapitalallokation und Wertschöpfung wider. Helen Giza, Vorstandsvorsitzende von Fresenius Medical Care AG, sagte: „Das neue Aktienrückkaufprogramm unterstreicht unser entschlossenes Engagement, Wert zu schaffen und Kapital an unsere Aktionärinnen und Aktionäre zurückzuführen. Den Start eines neuen Aktienrückkaufprogramms kurz nach dem erfolgreichen und früher als geplant abgeschlossenen vorherigen Aktienrückkaufprogramm über 1 Milliarde Euro verkünden zu können, zeigt unsere finanzielle Stärke und disziplinierte Umsetzung. title: AI Video is finally good enough. Now comes the hard part.
summary: Why the future of AI video isn’t about better clips, but better workflows
body_text: Wondercraft is becoming the AI video studio for real work. When we started Wondercraft, we thought we were building an audio company. We wanted to help anyone turn text into sound: podcasts, ads, meditations, narrations. If you could write it, you could make it sound good. And it worked. People all over the world used Wondercraft to tell stories, train teams, and ship content faster. But over time, something became obvious. The internet doesn’t really run on audio. The internet runs on video. And over the last year, something else became obvious too: AI video crossed a quality threshold. Suddenly, with new models coming out every few months, generating video is no longer the hard part. But using it… is. The strange moment AI video is in If you follow AI, it probably feels like video just exploded. Sora. Veo. A dozen other models. Every week, a new demo that looks impossible. And yet, when we talk to real teams, marketing, L&D, HR, comms, we hear the same thing: “We can generate cool stuff. We can’t ship it.” They have clips. They have experiments. They have folders full of “AI tests”. What they do not have is a reliable way to produce real videos for training, onboarding, internal updates, product launches, or social content. Video generation is no longer the bottleneck. Making it usable is. The clip problem Most AI video tools today are built around a simple idea: prompt → clip. And that’s impressive. But that’s not how work happens. Real video needs to be on brand, editable, reviewable, and repeatable across a team. A cool clip is not a workflow. A cool clip is not a system. A cool clip is not production. Most AI video tools generate clips. Businesses need outcomes. We’ve seen this pattern before First, new technology is magical. Then it’s chaotic. Then someone turns it into a system. That’s what happened with design tools, developer tools, and collaboration tools. AI video is entering that phase now. Avatars were the first wave. They proved companies were ready to use AI video. But now that visuals can be so much richer, the real challenge is no longer “can we generate this?” It’s: can we actually use this, every week, with real teams, for real work? What we decided to build About a year ago, we made a big internal decision. We didn’t want to build another AI toy. We wanted to build the AI video studio teams actually rely on. That meant a few things: Stop thinking in prompts Start thinking in outcomes Stop exposing raw tools Start building workflows Training video is not the same as a product launch. An internal update is not the same as a social ad. A highlight reel is not the same as a narrated explainer. Each of these has a structure. A logic. A set of decisions that matter. So we built Wondercraft around that. Meet the new Wondercraft Today, Wondercraft is an AI video studio that brings together: The best AI models across video, images, voice, music, sound, and text A real editor for control, timing, and branding And Wonda , our AI agent that orchestrates everything Instead of starting from a blank timeline or a blank prompt, you start from what you want to make: Explain and educate (training, onboarding, internal updates, docs to video) Promote and launch (product launches, announcements, ads, social videos) Polish existing content (cutdowns, localisation, highlight reels, cleanup) You make a few decisions. Wondercraft generates a strong first draft. And then you refine. Wonda doesn’t replace editing. It makes creation productive. The three layers Under the hood, Wondercraft is built on three layers: The Models The Studio Workflows (powered by Wonda) Outcome-driven flows that encode best practices and generate strong first drafts. A real editor for when details, timing, and branding matter. Best-in-class AI across video, images, voice, music, sound, and text — orchestrated behind the scenes, not dumped on the user. The goal isn’t to show you more AI. The goal is to help you ship more video. Who this is for We are building Wondercraft primarily for marketing, communications, enablement, HR, and L&D teams. Teams that need to produce video regularly, quickly, and on brand, without turning video into a specialised skill. We also see agencies and AI-native creators using Wondercraft as a powerful studio. But the core mission is simple: If the content has a job to do inside a business, Wondercraft should be able to make it. Where this goes AI models will keep changing. That’s a given. There will be better video models, better voice models, better everything. What matters more is what people can actually do with them. We don’t think the long-term winners in this space will just be the companies building models. They’ll be the companies teams trust to turn all of this into something usable inside real workflows. That’s the layer we’re trying to build with Wondercraft. AI video is already powerful. But without structure, it mostly creates noise. Our job is to turn that power into something teams can rely on. Starting today, Wondercraft is fully an AI video studio. You can start from footage, from a script, from a document, or from just an idea, and turn it into something you can actually ship. For us, this feels less like a pivot and more like the product finally becoming what it was always trying to be. We’re excited to see what you build with it.

title: Lilly to present Alzheimer's disease diagnostic and therapeutic research at AAIC 2026, including new data on P-tau217 blood tests and amyloid-targeting treatment
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Eli Lilly and Company's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Analyses across Kisunla (donanemab-azbt) trials providing further insights into the benefit-risk profile from long-term extension data New data compares the diagnostic performance of P-tau217 blood tests with amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) in cognitively unimpaired Alzheimer's disease Research spanning diagnostics, long-term treatment, disease biology, and patient-centered outcomes reflects Lilly's 35-year commitment to Alzheimer's disease science INDIANAPOLIS , July 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced it will present 16 abstracts at the 2026 Alzheimer's Association International Conference (AAIC), July 12-15 in London. Three oral presentations anchor the scientific program, with 13 poster presentations spanning imaging science, health economics, real-world prescribing evidence, and patient-centered outcomes, reflecting Lilly's 35-year commitment to answering open questions in Alzheimer's disease. Key Presentations at AAIC 2026 New Clinical Evidence on Kisunla (donanemab-azbt) On July 15, a Developing Topics Session, Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer's Disease: Evidence to Address Clinical Questions, will present new insights from TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 6 and the TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 long-term extension. Findings include new data on safety through modified titration and corticosteroid pretreatment as well as long-term extension evidence on biomarkers and the potential durability of clinical benefit. Advancing Diagnostics Also on July 15, Samantha Burnham, Ph.D., senior research scientist, Eli Lilly and Company, will present data showing P-tau217 blood biomarker assays demonstrated strong rule-in performance comparable to amyloid PET for identifying Alzheimer's disease pathology in cognitively unimpaired individuals. Though blood biomarker tests and amyloid PET agents are not currently indicated for use in cognitively unimpaired individuals, the results generate support for a potentially scalable, accessible alternative to specialized imaging in the future. Advancing Scientific Methodology On July 13, as the organizer of the Featured Research Session, Lars Raket, Ph.D., Eli Lilly and Company, will deliver an oral presentation on external controls versus internal extrapolation in the TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 long-term extension (Room N10). The analysis addresses a key methodological question in Alzheimer's disease research: how long-term outcomes are measured and interpreted in clinical trials, reflecting Lilly's commitment to the scientific rigor that underpins credible long-term evidence generation. A full list of abstracts appears below. Presentations will be available at www.lilly.com following their scheduled release times. disease, rising from approximately 55 million today, from those living with the earliest changes associated with the disease, to those experiencing profound memory loss.¹ The disease begins silently, often decades before any change in memory or thinking, with the accumulation of amyloid plaques in the brain,2 progressing through stages of increasing memory loss, behavioral changes, and growing dependence on caregivers.3 Nearly 4 in 5 Americans say they would want to know if they had Alzheimer's disease before experiencing symptoms or before symptoms interfere with their daily activities.4 About Kisunla® (donanemab-azbt) Kisunla is currently approved as an amyloid-targeting treatment for people with mild cognitive impairment as well as people with mild dementia stage of early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease with confirmed amyloid pathology. Kisunla is a humanized monoclonal antibody that targets and reduces insoluble N-truncated pyroglutamate amyloid beta plaques, a defining feature of Alzheimer's disease, and is administered as an intravenous infusion every four weeks. Kisunla can cause serious side effects, including ARIA and infusion-related reactions. Apolipoprotein E ε4 (ApoE ε4) homozygotes have a higher incidence of ARIA, including symptomatic and serious ARIA, and testing for ApoE ε4 status should be performed prior to initiating treatment. Carriers of one or two copies of the ApoE ε4 gene may be at higher risk of developing Alzheimer's disease and experiencing ARIA. Patients should discuss any safety concerns with their healthcare providers. INDICATION AND SAFETY SUMMARY WITH WARNINGS Kisunla® (kih-SUHN-lah) is used to treat adults with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease (AD), which includes mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or mild dementia stage of disease. Warnings - Kisunla can cause Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities or "ARIA." This is a common side effect that does not usually cause any symptoms, but serious symptoms can occur. ARIA can be fatal. ARIA is most commonly seen as temporary swelling in an area or areas of the brain that usually goes away over time. Some people may also have spots of bleeding on the surface of or in the brain and infrequently, larger areas of bleeding in the brain can occur. Although most people do not have symptoms, some people have: Headache Dizziness Nausea Difficulty walking Confusion Vision changes Seizures Some people have a genetic risk factor (homozygous apolipoprotein E ε4 gene carriers) that may cause an increased risk for ARIA. Talk to your healthcare provider about testing to see if you have this risk factor. You may be at higher risk of developing bleeding in the brain if you take medicines to reduce blood clots from forming (antithrombotic medicines) while receiving Kisunla. Talk to your healthcare provider to see if you are on any medicines that increase this risk. Your healthcare provider will do magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain scans before and during your treatment with Kisunla to check you for ARIA. You should carry information that you are receiving Kisunla, which can cause ARIA, and that ARIA symptoms can look like stroke symptoms. Call your healthcare provider or go to the nearest hospital emergency room right away if you have any of the symptoms listed above. There are registries that collect information on treatments for Alzheimer's disease. Your healthcare provider can help you become enrolled in these registries. Warnings - Kisunla can cause serious allergic and infusion-related reactions. Do not receive Kisunla if you have serious allergic reactions to donanemab-azbt or any of the ingredients in Kisunla. Symptoms may include swelling of the face, lips, mouth, or eyelids, problems breathing, hives, chills, irritation of skin, nausea, vomiting, sweating, headache, or chest pain. You will be monitored for at least 30 minutes after you receive Kisunla for any reaction. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have these symptoms or any reaction during or after a Kisunla infusion. Other common side effects Headache Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have any side effects. These are not all of the possible side effects of Kisunla. You can report side effects at 1-800-FDA-1088 or www.fda.gov/medwatch . Before you receive Kisunla, tell your healthcare provider: About all medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, as well as vitamins and herbal supplements. Especially tell your healthcare provider if you have medicines to reduce blood clots from forming (antithrombotic medicines, including aspirin). About all of your medical conditions including if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or plan to become pregnant or breastfeed. Kisunla has not been studied in people who were pregnant or breastfeeding. It is not known if Kisunla could harm your unborn or breastfeeding baby. How to receive Kisunla Kisunla is a prescription medicine given through an intravenous (IV) infusion using a needle inserted into a vein in your arm. Kisunla is given once every 4 weeks. Each infusion will last about 30 minutes. Learn more For more information about Kisunla, call 1-800-LillyRx (1-800-545-5979) or go to kisunla.lilly.com . This summary provides basic information about Kisunla. It does not include all information known about this medicine. Read the information given to you about Kisunla. This information does not take the place of talking with your healthcare provider. Be sure to talk to your healthcare provider about Kisunla. Your healthcare provider is the best person to help you decide if Kisunla is right for you.
